title: Isolate canonical reconstruction as the bounded packed-bitset hotspot

masterplan.active_gate: Gate 1 — Renovation, owner-directed Genesis and general computer assistance

scope: Use retained exact-head CI artifacts from the existing bounded CPU packed-bitset and TypedRelationBlock validation diagnostics to identify one measured sparse computational hotspot. Do not add a backend, cache, block type, delta abstraction or production optimization in this packet; first establish reproducible evidence about where canonical output materialization costs reside.

measurement.authority: diagnostic only; KnowledgeForest/Fourfold remain semantic authority and TypedRelationBlock.matmul remains the Boolean CSR oracle

validation_profile.interpretation: cProfile values are attribution evidence only and are not compared as absolute wall time against the unprofiled constructor. The independent unprofiled measurements establish the reconstruction hotspot; the profile indicates that TypedRelationBlock.__post_init__ dominates the profiled constructor path while persisted-scalar sequence admission is a minority component.

measurement.finding: For the frozen 256x256, row-width-13 case with 43,264 output entries, canonical reconstruction costs 2.686 ms versus 0.451 ms for the resident packed-bitset kernel. Reconstruction is about 5.96x the kernel phase; direct block construction is about 65.6% of reconstruction and support decoding about 34.4%. This isolates canonical output materialization, not Boolean relation composition, as the dominant measured post-kernel cost in this bounded case.
measurement.scope_limit: The diagnostic is synthetic, CPU-only and bounded. It does not establish a general speedup, memory win, production workload crossover, GPU/Tensor-Core superiority, or Tensor-over-Forest advantage.

No production optimization is made until that existing constructor owner is measured more finely without changing semantic admission.
